episode_title: #21 - Epirocs ordf. Ronnie Leten tillika en av Europas främsta företagsledare berättar om sina närmare 40 år inom Wallenbergssfären

recommendations.speaker: Ronnie Leten
recommendations.reasoning: India is highlighted as an interesting market with significant potential. It's described as the world's largest democracy with 1.5 billion people, having made big strides in infrastructure and education over the last 10 years. Compared to China 20 years ago, it's seen as a way to spread risks and leverage a democratic environment. The market is viewed as having huge potential for growth.
recommendations.quote: I think they have, if you look at their journey over the last 20, 30 years, it's fantastic. And especially the last 10 years, they have done a big step forwards in strengthening their infrastructure, their education system... And the advantage is, I think, of course, China 20, 25 years ago, I think we call it as the factory of the world. But of course, we all have learned that to put all our eggs in one basket is maybe not the best way. So from that point of view is India, which is a more democratic environment, which is maybe a better possibility, or we can spread our risks. And on the other hand, it is a huge, huge market, a huge potential market.

stock_segments.discussion_summary: Epiroc is a focused mining and infrastructure construction company spun off from Atlas Copco in 2018. It's a market leader in underground rock excavation with strong aftermarket business (68% of revenue). The company is investing heavily in automation, digitization, and electrification. Average operating margin 2015-2023 was 21.8%, far ahead of competitors at 11.7% due to asset-light model. Mining constitutes 83% of orders, infrastructure 17%. Revenue is geographically diverse with Asia/Australia at 30%. The company has an R&D focus with over 1,800 engineers.

quotes.speaker: Ronnie Leten
quotes.text: Epiroc is a focused company on mining and infrastructure construction. So it is a dedicated organization, which is globally, worldwide. Of course, the highest density is where the mines are.

quotes.speaker: Ronnie Leten
quotes.text: Availability is extremely important... And that is what I think we made. That came out partly on Atlas Copco, but we made a big quantum leap on the focus for aftermarket or service in the mid-2000s, where we really say aftermarket is a business, is a product, service is a product.

quotes.speaker: Ronnie Leten
quotes.text: If you look, if you think the mining part, I think look to the commodity prices, they are increased, so they're high. And what does it mean that the mine can make money? And when your customers are making money, they can invest, and that's the business where we are in.

quotes.speaker: Ronnie Leten
quotes.text: We differentiate in three things. First, we have the best team, the best people. And these best people make the best products, so the most innovative products and deliver the best service. So these are the three.

quotes.speaker: Ronnie Leten
quotes.text: Sell to customers who make money. That's simple. So when a mine, and you look to the BHPs and the Anglos of this world, they make good profit. That means they have, yeah, they have the ability to invest, to expand, to do further automation, to do whatever.

bull_case: Strong aftermarket business providing recurring revenue with higher margins
Market leader in underground rock excavation with best equipment and service
Asset-light business model allows agility through cycles
Beneficiary of copper demand increase due to electrification and digitalization
Automation and electrification trends create productivity opportunities
Exposure to growing markets like India
bear_case: Infrastructure sector currently in down cycle
Long lead times for new mines (15 years) could delay growth
Adoption of automation and electrification may be slower than expected
catalysts: Copper demand from electrification and AI
Infrastructure recovery when interest rates normalize
Mining customers investing in new equipment as fleet ages
risks: Slow adoption rates for new technologies

insights.quote: I think first, I think spending time with customers and products and not keeping busy with internal reorganizations, that's part. Then I think a second one is focusing on future businesses. When the businesses were not good, either you fix them or you sell them or you divest them.
insights.summary: Focus on customers and products rather than internal restructuring, and either fix or divest underperforming businesses.
insights.speaker: Ronnie Leten

insights.quote: When we say yes, we mean yes and we go for it. That is for me, that's one of the values. And I think the second one is high level of transparency.
insights.summary: Commitment means following through on promises, and transparency is essential for organizational trust.
insights.speaker: Ronnie Leten

insights.quote: There is always a better way. I'm glad, but not satisfied.
insights.summary: Continuous improvement mindset - always look for better ways even when things are going well.
insights.speaker: Ronnie Leten

insights.quote: My first, always my first advice I do is manage your private life. I think it is very difficult if you don't feel well for whatever you feel... It is very difficult to lead. It's very difficult if you don't feel well, if you don't feel focused, but relaxed and then work together with people.
insights.summary: Personal well-being and work-life balance are fundamental to effective leadership.
insights.speaker: Ronnie Leten

insights.quote: The best investment they can do is study. That's for sure.
insights.summary: Investment in education and personal development is the most valuable long-term investment.
insights.speaker: Ronnie Leten

insights.quote: I am believing in equity, because I think if we don't believe in equity, that means that we think that the world is shrinking.
insights.summary: Equity investing reflects belief in economic growth and a growing world.
insights.speaker: Ronnie Leten

insights.quote: Sell to customers who make money. That's simple. So when a mine, and you look to the BHPs and the Anglos of this world, they make good profit. That means they have, yeah, they have the ability to invest, to expand, to do further automation, to do whatever. And that is of course music for say, for providers like us. So yeah, I think always to be in a business where your customers are making money is the best place to be.
insights.summary: Focus on serving profitable customers who have capacity to invest and grow.
insights.speaker: Ronnie Leten

insights.quote: To build up a new factory, it takes you a year, two years, but to build a new mine and to build it up and going, it takes you 15 years. So you need to have forward looking, really forward looking.
insights.summary: Long-term thinking is critical due to long lead times in developing new mines.
insights.speaker: Ronnie Leten

summary: This episode features an interview with Ronnie Leten, Chairman of Epiroc and former CEO of Atlas Copco, discussing his 39-year career within the Wallenberg sphere. The conversation covers leadership principles, corporate culture at Atlas Copco and Epiroc, the importance of aftermarket business, and trends in mining and infrastructure including automation and electrification. Leten emphasizes the value of transparency, continuous improvement, and focusing on customers who make money. He shares insights on India's potential as a market and discusses Epiroc's strong operating margins despite the cyclical nature of mining.
key_takeaways: Epiroc has strong margins (21.8% avg) due to asset-light model and aftermarket focus
Mining is benefitting from copper demand due to electrification and AI trends
Automation and electrification are key trends that will transform mining over the next 10 years
India represents significant long-term market potential similar to China 20 years ago
Leadership principles include commitment, transparency, and focusing on customers and products
